import numpy as np,pandas as pd
from lmfit.models import LorentzianModel,LinearModel
def fit(f,cens,lo,hi,names):
    d=pd.read_csv(f);m=(d.shift_cm1>lo)&(d.shift_cm1<hi);x=d.shift_cm1[m].values;y=d.intensity[m].values
    mod=LinearModel(prefix='b_');pars=mod.make_params(slope=0,intercept=np.median(y))
    for i,(c,n) in enumerate(zip(cens,names)):
        l=LorentzianModel(prefix=f'p{i}_');pars.update(l.make_params(center=c,sigma=4,amplitude=2000));pars[f'p{i}_center'].min=c-8;pars[f'p{i}_center'].max=c+8;pars[f'p{i}_sigma'].min=0.8;pars[f'p{i}_sigma'].max=15;mod+=l
    r=mod.fit(y,pars,x=x)
    print(f,lo,hi,'redchi',r.redchi)
    for i,n in enumerate(names):
        p=r.params
        print(' ',n,round(p[f'p{i}_center'].value,2),'±',round(p[f'p{i}_center'].stderr or 0,2),'FWHM',round(2*p[f'p{i}_sigma'].value,1),'H',round(p[f'p{i}_height'].value,0),'A',round(p[f'p{i}_amplitude'].value))
    return r

content.text: The data are fitted and I'm writing up the report now. Spot 1 looks like a monolayer or very thin WS2, and spot 2 looks like thick or bulk-like WS2.

input.summary: Spot 1 is consistent with monolayer (1L) WS2 and spot 2 with thick or bulk-like 2H-WS2. At 514.5 nm the spot 1 band at ~351 cm-1 is dominated by the resonantly enhanced 2LA(M) mode, with the in-plane E' (E2g) mode only a weak shoulder at ~355 cm-1. A1' (A1g) sits at 417.3 cm-1, the E'–A1' spacing is ~62 cm-1, and 2LA/A1' is ~2.2 in height and ~4.4 in area. Spot 2 has A1g at 420.1 cm-1, E2g at 355.4 cm-1, a spacing of ~64.7 cm-1, and 2LA/A1g of ~0.7 in height and ~0.9 in area. This is strong evidence for monolayer, but a bilayer is not excluded without PL or AFM. The Raman-based assignment is "1L (possibly 1–2L)".

observations.finding: Peak assignment (both spots): ~176 cm-1 is LA(M); ~350–351 cm-1 is the 2LA(M) second-order band; ~355 cm-1 is E'/E2g (in-plane, Gamma point); 417–420 cm-1 is A1'/A1g (out-of-plane); 520.8 cm-1 is the Si substrate. The weak features in spot 2 at ~195, ~225 and ~266 cm-1 are most likely second-order or combination modes.
observations.evidence: Lorentzian fits over 150–450 cm-1. Spot 1: LA ~176.0 (FWHM ~10), 2LA 351.1±0.1 (FWHM 9.0), E' 355.3±0.1 (FWHM 3.9), A1' 417.28±0.02 (FWHM 4.5). Spot 2: LA ~175.6, 2LA 349.9±0.1 (FWHM 8.8), E2g 355.4±0.04 (FWHM 4.1), A1g 420.08±0.02 (FWHM 4.4). Si 520.9 cm-1 in spot 1 and 520.8 cm-1 in spot 2 (FWHM 3.5), so the calibration is good. The weak spot 2 peaks come from peak-finding only and were not fitted.

observations.finding: A1(g) stiffens by ~2.8 cm-1 from spot 1 to spot 2. The E'/E2g position barely changes. The A1–E spacing is the usual thickness ruler and grows from ~62 to ~64.7 cm-1.
The 2LA(M)/A1g intensity ratio is the strongest monolayer indicator at this wavelength. Spot 1 is dominated by 2LA(M), while in spot 2 2LA and E2g are comparable to or weaker than A1g.
observations.evidence: Spot 1: 2LA/A1' ~2.2 by peak height (1807 vs 806 counts) and ~4.4 by fitted area (25483 vs 5750). Spot 2: ~0.7 by height (527 vs 1134) and ~0.9 by area (7244 vs 7838). That is a ~5-fold drop in the area ratio. The 351 band in spot 1 is asymmetric on the high-energy side, which is the buried E' at ~355 cm-1. The area ratio is model-dependent.

observations.finding: Thick spot 2 shows a resolved 2LA(M)/E2g doublet (350 and 355 cm-1). Spot 1 shows a single asymmetric band because E' is weak relative to 2LA.
observations.evidence: Spot 2 has a clear shoulder at ~349–350 cm-1 on the 355.4 cm-1 peak. In spot 1 the fitted E' height is ~410 counts against a 2LA height of ~1800 (ratio ~0.23). In spot 2 the E2g height is ~670 against a 2LA height of ~530 (ratio ~1.3).

observations.finding: The Si 520.8 cm-1 signal is ~10 times stronger at spot 1 than at spot 2, consistent with spot 1 being much thinner and more transparent at 514.5 nm.
observations.evidence: Si peak height above baseline ~1240 counts at spot 1 against ~120 at spot 2. Si FWHM is 3.5 cm-1 in both. This is a qualitative support only, because interference with the SiO2 layer and focus also change it.

observations.finding: Literature position and spacing for WS2 layer-number dependence at ~514 nm.
observations.evidence: The A1g position, the E–A1g spacing and the 2LA/A1g intensity ratio all trend with layer number. I give the monolayer values as approximately E' ~356 and A1' ~417 cm-1, and bulk values as E2g ~356 and A1g ~420–421 cm-1. These values are quoted from memory and not re-checked against the papers in this session. Our spot 1 and spot 2 match them.
observations.source: Berkdemir et al., Sci. Rep. 3, 1755 (2013), Figs. 2–4. Zhao et al., Nanoscale 5, 9677 (2013), Fig. 2.

caveats: 514.5 nm (2.41 eV) is near the B exciton of WS2 and gives resonant enhancement. The 2LA(M) intensity is strongly resonance-dependent: it is enhanced on the monolayer, and the enhancement is thickness-dependent. Absolute intensity ratios are therefore valid only for this laser line and cannot be transferred to other excitation energies. Do not use E/A1 intensity ratios across different wavelengths.

The E' mode in spot 1 is buried under the much stronger 2LA(M) band. Its fitted position (355.3 cm-1) and width depend on the model, and on the 2LA/E' split and the constraints. The A1'–E' spacing of ~62 cm-1 therefore has an uncertainty of order 1 cm-1. The A1' position is much better determined.

The spacing and A1g position distinguish 1L from bulk well but do not cleanly separate 1L from 2L. Several layer-dependent signatures overlap for 1L and 2L in WS2 (spacing, 2LA/A1g ratio), so use PL and low-frequency modes to separate them.

A1g shifts with doping, strain, substrate coupling and laser heating, as well as with layer number. CVD monolayers on SiO2 are often n-doped and may have residual strain from growth, which could shift A1' by ~1 cm-1 by itself. Spot-to-spot differences of 1–2 cm-1 are not purely a thickness effect.
The Si 520.8 cm-1 intensity depends on the SiO2 thickness (interference), focus and laser spot position. It supports spot 1 being thinner, but is not a thickness measurement.
The weak features at ~195, ~225 and ~266 cm-1 in spot 2 were identified only by peak-finding with ~3% prominence. They are close to the noise and were not fitted or assigned definitively.
Spot 1 and spot 2 are single-point spectra. Island uniformity, edge versus centre effects and multilayer nuclei (common at the centre of CVD triangles) are not covered.
questions_for_user: Is the PL spectrum available for spot 1? A single strong A-exciton PL peak at ~2.0 eV (~620 nm) with no indirect-gap shoulder would settle 1L vs 2L, because Raman here cannot do so cleanly.
What laser power and objective were used? Laser heating and local doping affect the A1' position and width, and the power determines whether the shift to 417.3 cm-1 is partly thermal.
Is there an AFM height or optical contrast measurement of the island? A ~0.7–0.8 nm step height would confirm a monolayer. Optical contrast on 90 vs 285 nm SiO2 gives a quick check.
What is the SiO2 thickness? The Si 520.8 cm-1 intensity and the resonance enhancement depend on the interference with this layer.
Were the spectra taken in the island centre, and is there any bilayer nucleation or multilayer centre in the triangle? CVD triangular islands often have thicker cores.
Do you have low-frequency (<50 cm-1) data? Interlayer shear and breathing modes would directly count layers and tell 1L from 2L, since they are absent in the monolayer.
Is the incident and scattered polarisation configuration known? In parallel polarisation E' and A1' intensities change, which would affect the ratios quoted here.
citations: Berkdemir, A. et al. Identification of individual and few layers of WS2 using Raman spectroscopy. Sci. Rep. 3, 1755 (2013): Figs. 2–4, layer dependence of E, 2LA(M) and A1g, and 2LA/A1g intensity.
Zhao, W. et al. Lattice dynamics in mono- and few-layer sheets of WS2 and WSe2. Nanoscale 5, 9677 (2013): Fig. 2, layer-dependent peak positions.
limits: The data are two single-point spectra at one laser line (514.5 nm) and one temperature (295 K). They cannot give an absolute layer count, only a ranking (spot 1 thinner than spot 2) plus consistency with monolayer. They cannot separate 1L from 2L, or give a thickness for the thick spot 2 beyond 'bulk-like'.
They cannot determine doping, strain or substrate coupling separately: the A1' position mixes these with layer number, and E' is too weak and overlapped in spot 1 to give a reliable strain estimate.
No information on lateral homogeneity, island edges, grain boundaries or stacking order, since only two points were measured and there is no low-frequency data.
Literature reference values are quoted from memory and have not been re-checked against the papers in this session.

structured_output.summary: Spot 1 is consistent with monolayer (1L) WS2 and spot 2 with thick or bulk-like 2H-WS2. At 514.5 nm the spot 1 band at ~351 cm-1 is dominated by the resonantly enhanced 2LA(M) mode, with the in-plane E' (E2g) mode only a weak shoulder at ~355 cm-1. A1' (A1g) sits at 417.3 cm-1, the E'–A1' spacing is ~62 cm-1, and 2LA/A1' is ~2.2 in height and ~4.4 in area. Spot 2 has A1g at 420.1 cm-1, E2g at 355.4 cm-1, a spacing of ~64.7 cm-1, and 2LA/A1g of ~0.7 in height and ~0.9 in area. This is strong evidence for monolayer, but a bilayer is not excluded without PL or AFM. The Raman-based assignment is "1L (possibly 1–2L)".

observations.finding: Peak assignment (both spots): ~176 cm-1 is LA(M); ~350–351 cm-1 is the 2LA(M) second-order band; ~355 cm-1 is E'/E2g (in-plane, Gamma point); 417–420 cm-1 is A1'/A1g (out-of-plane); 520.8 cm-1 is the Si substrate. The weak features in spot 2 at ~195, ~225 and ~266 cm-1 are most likely second-order or combination modes.
observations.evidence: Lorentzian fits over 150–450 cm-1. Spot 1: LA ~176.0 (FWHM ~10), 2LA 351.1±0.1 (FWHM 9.0), E' 355.3±0.1 (FWHM 3.9), A1' 417.28±0.02 (FWHM 4.5). Spot 2: LA ~175.6, 2LA 349.9±0.1 (FWHM 8.8), E2g 355.4±0.04 (FWHM 4.1), A1g 420.08±0.02 (FWHM 4.4). Si 520.9 cm-1 in spot 1 and 520.8 cm-1 in spot 2 (FWHM 3.5), so the calibration is good. The weak spot 2 peaks come from peak-finding only and were not fitted.

observations.finding: A1(g) stiffens by ~2.8 cm-1 from spot 1 to spot 2. The E'/E2g position barely changes. The A1–E spacing is the usual thickness ruler and grows from ~62 to ~64.7 cm-1.
The 2LA(M)/A1g intensity ratio is the strongest monolayer indicator at this wavelength. Spot 1 is dominated by 2LA(M), while in spot 2 2LA and E2g are comparable to or weaker than A1g.
observations.evidence: Spot 1: 2LA/A1' ~2.2 by peak height (1807 vs 806 counts) and ~4.4 by fitted area (25483 vs 5750). Spot 2: ~0.7 by height (527 vs 1134) and ~0.9 by area (7244 vs 7838). That is a ~5-fold drop in the area ratio. The 351 band in spot 1 is asymmetric on the high-energy side, which is the buried E' at ~355 cm-1. The area ratio is model-dependent.

observations.finding: Thick spot 2 shows a resolved 2LA(M)/E2g doublet (350 and 355 cm-1). Spot 1 shows a single asymmetric band because E' is weak relative to 2LA.
observations.evidence: Spot 2 has a clear shoulder at ~349–350 cm-1 on the 355.4 cm-1 peak. In spot 1 the fitted E' height is ~410 counts against a 2LA height of ~1800 (ratio ~0.23). In spot 2 the E2g height is ~670 against a 2LA height of ~530 (ratio ~1.3).

observations.finding: The Si 520.8 cm-1 signal is ~10 times stronger at spot 1 than at spot 2, consistent with spot 1 being much thinner and more transparent at 514.5 nm.
observations.evidence: Si peak height above baseline ~1240 counts at spot 1 against ~120 at spot 2. Si FWHM is 3.5 cm-1 in both. This is a qualitative support only, because interference with the SiO2 layer and focus also change it.

observations.finding: Literature position and spacing for WS2 layer-number dependence at ~514 nm.
observations.evidence: The A1g position, the E–A1g spacing and the 2LA/A1g intensity ratio all trend with layer number. I give the monolayer values as approximately E' ~356 and A1' ~417 cm-1, and bulk values as E2g ~356 and A1g ~420–421 cm-1. These values are quoted from memory and not re-checked against the papers in this session. Our spot 1 and spot 2 match them.
observations.source: Berkdemir et al., Sci. Rep. 3, 1755 (2013), Figs. 2–4. Zhao et al., Nanoscale 5, 9677 (2013), Fig. 2.

caveats: 514.5 nm (2.41 eV) is near the B exciton of WS2 and gives resonant enhancement. The 2LA(M) intensity is strongly resonance-dependent: it is enhanced on the monolayer, and the enhancement is thickness-dependent. Absolute intensity ratios are therefore valid only for this laser line and cannot be transferred to other excitation energies. Do not use E/A1 intensity ratios across different wavelengths.

The E' mode in spot 1 is buried under the much stronger 2LA(M) band. Its fitted position (355.3 cm-1) and width depend on the model, and on the 2LA/E' split and the constraints. The A1'–E' spacing of ~62 cm-1 therefore has an uncertainty of order 1 cm-1. The A1' position is much better determined.

The spacing and A1g position distinguish 1L from bulk well but do not cleanly separate 1L from 2L. Several layer-dependent signatures overlap for 1L and 2L in WS2 (spacing, 2LA/A1g ratio), so use PL and low-frequency modes to separate them.

A1g shifts with doping, strain, substrate coupling and laser heating, as well as with layer number. CVD monolayers on SiO2 are often n-doped and may have residual strain from growth, which could shift A1' by ~1 cm-1 by itself. Spot-to-spot differences of 1–2 cm-1 are not purely a thickness effect.
The Si 520.8 cm-1 intensity depends on the SiO2 thickness (interference), focus and laser spot position. It supports spot 1 being thinner, but is not a thickness measurement.
The weak features at ~195, ~225 and ~266 cm-1 in spot 2 were identified only by peak-finding with ~3% prominence. They are close to the noise and were not fitted or assigned definitively.
Spot 1 and spot 2 are single-point spectra. Island uniformity, edge versus centre effects and multilayer nuclei (common at the centre of CVD triangles) are not covered.
questions_for_user: Is the PL spectrum available for spot 1? A single strong A-exciton PL peak at ~2.0 eV (~620 nm) with no indirect-gap shoulder would settle 1L vs 2L, because Raman here cannot do so cleanly.
What laser power and objective were used? Laser heating and local doping affect the A1' position and width, and the power determines whether the shift to 417.3 cm-1 is partly thermal.
Is there an AFM height or optical contrast measurement of the island? A ~0.7–0.8 nm step height would confirm a monolayer. Optical contrast on 90 vs 285 nm SiO2 gives a quick check.
What is the SiO2 thickness? The Si 520.8 cm-1 intensity and the resonance enhancement depend on the interference with this layer.
Were the spectra taken in the island centre, and is there any bilayer nucleation or multilayer centre in the triangle? CVD triangular islands often have thicker cores.
Do you have low-frequency (<50 cm-1) data? Interlayer shear and breathing modes would directly count layers and tell 1L from 2L, since they are absent in the monolayer.
Is the incident and scattered polarisation configuration known? In parallel polarisation E' and A1' intensities change, which would affect the ratios quoted here.
citations: Berkdemir, A. et al. Identification of individual and few layers of WS2 using Raman spectroscopy. Sci. Rep. 3, 1755 (2013): Figs. 2–4, layer dependence of E, 2LA(M) and A1g, and 2LA/A1g intensity.
Zhao, W. et al. Lattice dynamics in mono- and few-layer sheets of WS2 and WSe2. Nanoscale 5, 9677 (2013): Fig. 2, layer-dependent peak positions.
limits: The data are two single-point spectra at one laser line (514.5 nm) and one temperature (295 K). They cannot give an absolute layer count, only a ranking (spot 1 thinner than spot 2) plus consistency with monolayer. They cannot separate 1L from 2L, or give a thickness for the thick spot 2 beyond 'bulk-like'.
They cannot determine doping, strain or substrate coupling separately: the A1' position mixes these with layer number, and E' is too weak and overlapped in spot 1 to give a reliable strain estimate.
No information on lateral homogeneity, island edges, grain boundaries or stacking order, since only two points were measured and there is no low-frequency data.
Literature reference values are quoted from memory and have not been re-checked against the papers in this session.
